function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal instruction or authorization that gives a party (often a financial institution) the authority to act on behalf of another party (the client). It’s essentially a contract that specifies what actions the authorized party may take, under what conditions, and for how long. Key points: | Aspect | Typical meaning | |--------|-----------------| | **Purpose** | Grants permission to perform specific tasks (e.g., execute trades, manage assets, make payments). | | **Parties involved** | *Client* (who gives the mandate) and *Mandate holder* (who receives it). | | **Legal nature** | Binding agreement; often governed by regulatory rules (e.g., MiFID II in the EU). | | **Status categories** | • **Active** – currently in force.
• **Pending** – awaiting approval or activation.
• **Inactive** – expired, revoked, or cancelled. | In practice, you’ll see mandates used for: - **Investment management** – a client authorizes a fund manager to trade on their behalf. - **Payment instructions** – a company gives a bank a mandate to debit its accounts automatically. - **Corporate governance** – a board may issue a mandate to a committee to carry out certain duties. So, when you hear “mandate” in finance or business, think of it as a legally binding instruction that empowers someone else to act for you.
